edges.description: The substituted residue changes how mutant HSPB8 engages its partner small heat shock protein.

Curated as the mechanistic link between the altered small heat shock protein interaction and the CASA pathway that HSPB8 serves. The sources here establish HSPB8's role in that pathway and the mutants' altered binding; they do not measure CASA flux in K141 HSPB8 motor neurons, so the edge is marked indirect.
Failure to clear misfolded clients leaves them to accumulate as aggregates.

Left deliberately uncited. The sources curated here assert protein aggregation and inclusion body formation as a pathogenic mechanism of dHMN as a class, but none of them demonstrates that K141 HSPB8 aggregates cause the degeneration of the longest motor axons.

nodes.description: Severe atrophy and wasting of distal limb muscles secondary to chronic denervation.

evidence.reference_title: Hot-spot residue in small heat-shock protein 22 causes distal motor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Distal hereditary motor neuropathies are pure motor disorders of the peripheral nervous system resulting in severe atrophy and wasting of distal limb muscles.

nodes.description: Slowly progressive, length-dependent weakness of distal limb muscles, the defining clinical feature of the distal hereditary motor neuropathies.

evidence.reference_title: Early onset hereditary neuronopathies: an update on non-5q motor neuron diseases.
evidence.snippet: slowly progressive length-dependent distal muscle weakness and atrophy, without sensory involvement

meta.association: Heterozygous missense variants at the K141 hot-spot residue in the alpha-crystallin domain of HSPB8. K141N was found in two dHMN type II pedigrees and K141E in two smaller families; the same residue is essential to the structural and functional integrity of alphaA-crystallin, and its mutation in other small heat shock proteins produces other human disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Hot-spot residue in small heat-shock protein 22 causes distal motor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: We found a second mutation (K141E) in two smaller families. Both mutations target the same amino acid, which is essential to the structural and functional integrity of the small heat-shock protein alphaA-crystallin.

The causative genes have implicated proteins with diverse functions such as protein misfolding (HSPB1, HSPB8, BSCL2), RNA metabolism (IGHMBP2, SETX, GARS), axonal transport (HSPB1, DYNC1H1, DCTN1) and cation-channel dysfunction (ATP7A and TRPV4) in motor-nerve disease.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense substitution of the K141 lysine in the alpha-crystallin domain of HSPB8. The two reported founding alleles, K141N and K141E, change the same positively charged residue, which is required for the structural and functional integrity of small heat shock proteins of this family.

evidence.reference_title: Hot-spot residue in small heat-shock protein 22 causes distal motor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: This positively charged residue, when mutated in other small heat-shock proteins, results in various human disorders.

genetic_context.description: Curated as a toxic gain of function rather than haploinsufficiency. The mutant protein binds its partner small heat shock protein more avidly than wild type and drives aggregate formation, which is an acquired behaviour rather than an absent one; a null allele would not explain either observation.

nodes.description: HSPB8 works with the co-chaperone BAG3 as the sub-complex at the base of chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA), which disposes of damaged and misfolded clients through Hsc70, the ubiquitin ligase CHIP and the autophagy adaptor p62. Disturbance of this complex is the proteostatic failure curated as the cellular lesion of dHMN2A. Note that the CASA machinery is characterised in muscle and in BAG3-mutant cell models rather than in K141-HSPB8 motor neurons.

biological_processes: protein ubiquitination by CHIP during CASA

evidence.reference_title: Chaperone-assisted selective autophagy is essential for muscle maintenance.
evidence.snippet: Stv and its mammalian ortholog BAG-3 coordinate the activity of Hsc70 and the small heat shock protein HspB8 during disposal that is initiated by the chaperone-associated ubiquitin ligase CHIP and the autophagic ubiquitin adaptor p62.

evidence.reference_title: BAG3 Pro209 mutants associated with myopathy and neuropathy relocate chaperones of the CASA-complex to aggresomes.
evidence.snippet: BAG3-HSPB8 is a sub-complex at the basis of a larger protein complex, known as the chaperone-assisted-selective-autophagy (CASA) complex.

nodes.description: Both K141 mutants coimmunoprecipitate more of the partner small heat shock protein HSPB1 than wild-type HSPB8 does, indicating an abnormally avid rather than an absent chaperone interaction.

evidence.reference_title: Hot-spot residue in small heat-shock protein 22 causes distal motor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Coimmunoprecipitation experiments showed greater binding of both HSPB8 mutants to the interacting partner HSPB1.

nodes.description: Expression of mutant HSPB8 promotes formation of intracellular aggregates in cultured cells. Protein aggregation and inclusion body formation is one of the recurring pathogenic mechanisms of the distal hereditary motor neuropathies as a group.

evidence.reference_title: Hot-spot residue in small heat-shock protein 22 causes distal motor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Expression of mutant HSPB8 in cultured cells promoted formation of intracellular aggregates.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular genetics and mechanisms of disease in distal hereditary motor neuropathies: insights directing future genetic studies.
evidence.snippet: These include disruption of axonal transport, RNA processing defects, protein aggregation and inclusion body formation, disrupted calcium channel activity, and loss of neuroprotective signalling.

nodes.description: Second missense substitution at the same codon, found in two smaller families.
Missense substitution of the hot-spot lysine at codon 141 in the alpha-crystallin domain, found in two dHMN type II pedigrees linked to 12q24.3.

Degeneration of the distal portions of the longest lower motor neuron axons, which is the lesion shared across the distal hereditary motor neuropathies and the reason weakness begins in the feet and progresses proximally.

evidence.snippet: The distal hereditary motor neuropathies (dHMN) comprise a heterogeneous group of diseases that share the common feature of a length-dependent predominantly motor neuropathy.
